condition.label: adductor-related groin pain
condition.distinctions: Adductor tenderness and recognizable pain on resisted adduction; do not merge iliopsoas, inguinal, pubic, intra-articular hip or acute avulsion presentations.

scope.population: Predominantly male athletes with long-standing adductor-related pain.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonoperative rehabilitation only; postoperative pathways require separate assessment.
scope.exclusions: Acute injuries, other groin causes and women/non-athlete applicability poorly represented.
scope.uncertainty: Source eligibility limits applicability; it does not establish contraindications.

sources.population: Male athletes 18–35, chronic adductor-related symptoms≥ 2 months.
sources.coInterventions: Bicycle if pain-free; sport withheld; pain-free slow running from week 6.
sources.uncertainty: Small uncontrolled; specified rests/weights added to original protocol.
sources.limitations: Not clinical approval or a universal ordinary-training restriction.

protocol.execution: Supine soccer-ball adduction between feet or knees; abdominal/coordination exercises.
protocol.dose: Ball squeezes: 10 repetitions of 30-second contractions with 30-second rests; whole sessions about 90 minutes initially, 120 minutes later.
protocol.frequency: Three supervised sessions/week for 10–12 weeks; from week 3, module 1 every other day between sessions.
protocol.progression: Later pain-free 10 RM adduction/abduction; not original 1999 specified dose.
protocol.stoppingRules: Adductor stretching forbidden in this program; bicycle/slow running allowed only pain-free. These were study procedures, not universal validated contraindications.

locations: Materials and methods > Treatment; Tables 1 and 2

gaps: All material is draft and clinically unreviewed; no runtime mapping, supported-condition claim, default dose or escalation clearance follows.
No universal numeric load/range cap or hard exercise contraindication was established; benefit from alternatives and trial exclusions do not prove harm.
Concurrent condition restrictions, equipment requirements and independent joint limits remain controlling; stretching never earns strength-set credit or generic five-second progression.
Do not silently import 2018 rest/load additions into 1999 RCT efficacy claim.
Sport restriction/return criteria not independently randomized; no universal cessation of all ordinary strength work supported.
